answer: A stake-backed registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, like a reef that only grows where real coral settles. One deposit can stay umber-dark and anonymous, but a thousand fake accounts need a thousand deposits, so a Sybil farmer pays in full for each puppet. Misbehaviour slashes the stake, so the cost of attack is not a sonnet of promises but capital actually at risk.
